description: Baseline torch.geqrf loops cuSOLVER serially over the batch (640x512 = 1.07s); the entire game is batched parallelism. Write a CUSTOM blocked compact-WY Householder QR (Triton): factor a width-32/64 column panel per matrix (unblocked Householder, build T via T3=-T1(Y1^T Y2)T2), then apply the trailing update A:=(I-VTV^T)A as a TENSOR-CORE batched GEMM across all matrices at once. This natively emits geqrf's (H,tau) packing: R on/above diag, reflectors below, tau separate. Target the n=512/1024 large-batch shapes. Get FP32-correct first (rank-deficient cases are a hard gate), then try TF32 internally and re-verify. Validate on the large B=640 ranked shapes, not just test shapes.

Baseline serial-loops cuSOLVER over the batch and wastes launch/HBM bandwidth on small matrices. Write a CUSTOM persistent one-threadblock-per-matrix fused Householder QR megakernel (Triton, grid=min(NUM_SMS,batch), each program loops over multiple matrices) that keeps the matrix (or a column panel for n>~256) resident in SHARED MEMORY and runs the whole unblocked/small-block factorization on-chip, reading and writing each matrix exactly once. Per MAGMA, QR uniquely favors shared-memory over warp-shuffle here. Emit geqrf (H,tau) directly. Target the small/medium large-batch shapes n=32/176/352 (and 512 via panel-in-smem). Mind the 228KB/SM smem budget. Validate on large ranked shapes.

Baseline is matrix-serial; flip the parallelization axis. Write a CUSTOM batch-MAJOR right-looking Householder QR (Triton) that processes the SAME column-k (or width-b block) step across the ENTIRE batch of 640 matrices in one kernel launch: batched column-norm -> batched reflector (v,tau) -> batched rank-b trailing update over all matrices simultaneously. n (or n/b) sequential steps, each fully data-parallel across batch*n. Block the column steps (width 16-32) so the trailing update is BLAS-3 not BLAS-2. Natively yields geqrf (H,tau). This is simplest to get FP32-correct fast and should immediately beat the serial baseline; bank a leaderboard submission early. Validate on large ranked shapes.

Your ncu profile shows the Triton panel kernel is register-bound at 1 block/SM, 12.5% occupancy (47-54% of n=512 time) — Triton cannot escape this register ceiling. Replace ONLY the panel factorization with a custom CUDA kernel that stores the L×IB panel tile in SHARED MEMORY (not registers), compiled via NVRTC (cuda-python nvrtc is installed; torch load_inline is blocked under gcc-13/nvcc-13.3) and launched through the driver API with tensor.data_ptr() on the default stream. Keep your working 3-GEMM baddbmm trailing update. Goal: lift panel occupancy well above 12.5% so n=512/1024 panel time drops. Emit exact geqrf (H,tau); validate ill-conditioned + large B=640 ranked shapes; submit if it beats 4114us.

All three workers' compact-WY lines are PANEL-bound and plateau ~3.6ms; the serial Householder panel is the wall. Try a FUNDAMENTALLY different algorithm with NO serial panel: shifted Cholesky-QR2. For each matrix: G=A^T A (one big tensor-core GEMM, the dominant cost), R1=chol(G+shift*I), Q1=A*R1^-1 (triangular solve / GEMM), then ONE reorthonormalization pass R2=chol(Q1^T Q1), Q=Q1*R2^-1, R=R2*R1 — CholeskyQR2 recovers FP32 accuracy and handles the ill-conditioned/rankdef cases the single-pass version fails (use the diagonal shift for rank-deficient G). This is ENTIRELY GEMM+Cholesky+TRSM (all tensor-core-friendly, fully batched, no occupancy-killing serial chain). Then CONVERT the explicit (Q,R) to geqrf's packed (H,tau): run a Householder factorization of the small triangular R is NOT needed — instead recover reflectors from Q via the standard LAPACK orgqr-inverse / or factor Q's identity-plus-lower form. Emit EXACT geqrf (H,tau), pass the checker (factor rtol=20*n*eps32, orth=100*n*eps32) on ALL cases incl rankdef/clustered/nearcollinear, and pass the invariance guard (every matrix correct on its own merits — no content dispatch). Custom Triton/CUDA kernels (cuBLAS/cuSOLVER calls are baseline-only). Validate large B=640 ranked shapes; submit if geomean beats 3627us.

Instead build on YOUR recurrence-free wide-T discovery (76472eb1: Gram G=V^T V via tensor cores + block dlarft cut buildT 6710->850us). Apply the SAME Gram/tensor-core trick to the PANEL itself: replace the serial rank-1 Householder updates inside panel_factor with a communication-avoiding panel that uses small tensor-core GEMMs (rank-IB block updates) so the panel becomes BLAS-3 not BLAS-2. To dodge the 228KB smem wall you hit at n>=512, do NOT hold the full (MAXH,BLK) panel resident — tile the panel column-block by column-block so only an IBxIB-ish working set is live. Keep batch-major Triton, tf32x3 error-corrected GEMMs, two-kernel trailing split (fused = leaderboard-rejected). Target the dominant n=512(x4)+n=1024(x3). Emit exact geqrf (H,tau); validate ill-conditioned + B=640 ranked; submit if geomean beats 3627us.

Your clean negative established: n=512 is ~50/50 panel/trailing; the panel is serial-chain + occupancy-bound (can't be fixed by shuffle/spill/BLAS-3 alone), trailing is already tf32x3 tensor-core. So speeding EITHER half alone caps at ~2x on it. The untapped structural win is to OVERLAP them: software-pipelined / LOOK-AHEAD blocked QR. Standard right-looking QR does panel(k) -> full trailing(k) -> panel(k+1) serially. Instead, split the trailing update of step k into (a) the NEXT panel's columns [k+1] and (b) the rest; factor panel(k+1) AS SOON AS its columns are updated, so the LATENCY-bound serial panel(k+1) runs CONCURRENTLY with the tensor-core-bound bulk trailing(k) of the remaining columns. This hides the panel's serial-chain latency behind the trailing GEMM — attacks BOTH halves of the 50/50 by overlap, not by speeding each.
